From 8df672bfe3ec2268c2636584202755898e547173 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Oliver Neukum <oneukum@suse.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:01:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] usb: class: cdc-wdm: fix reordering issue in read code path

Quoting the bug report:

Due to compiler optimization or CPU out-of-order execution, the
desc->length update can be reordered before the memmove. If this
happens, wdm_read() can see the new length and call copy_to_user() on
uninitialized memory. This also violates LKMM data race rules [1].

Fix it by using WRITE_ONCE and memory barriers.

Fixes: afba937e540c9 ("USB: CDC WDM driver")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Oliver Neukum <oneukum@suse.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-usb/CALbr=LbrUZn_cfp7CfR-7Z5wDTHF96qeuM=3fO2m-q4cDrnC4A@mail.gmail.com/
Reported-by: Gui-Dong Han <hanguidong02@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Gui-Dong Han <hanguidong02@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260304130116.1721682-1-oneukum@suse.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/class/cdc-wdm.c b/drivers/usb/class/cdc-wdm.c
index f2d94cfc70af..7556c0dac908 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/class/cdc-wdm.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/class/cdc-wdm.c
@@ -225,7 +225,8 @@ static void wdm_in_callback(struct urb *urb)
 		/* we may already be in overflow */
 		if (!test_bit(WDM_OVERFLOW, &desc->flags)) {
 			memmove(desc->ubuf + desc->length, desc->inbuf, length);
-			desc->length += length;
+			smp_wmb(); /* against wdm_read() */
+			WRITE_ONCE(desc->length, desc->length + length);
 		}
 	}
 skip_error:
@@ -533,6 +534,7 @@ static ssize_t wdm_read
 		return -ERESTARTSYS;
 
 	cntr = READ_ONCE(desc->length);
+	smp_rmb(); /* against wdm_in_callback() */
 	if (cntr == 0) {
 		desc->read = 0;
 retry:
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Files Modified

1. **drivers/usb/class/cdc-wdm.c** (one file, two hunks)

   - **Hunk 1 – `wdm_in_callback()` (write side):**
     - Added `smp_wmb()` (write memory barrier) before the update of `desc->length`.
     - Changed the plain assignment `desc->length += length;` to `WRITE_ONCE(desc->length, desc->length + length);`.

   - **Hunk 2 – `wdm_read()` (read side):**
     - After the `READ_ONCE(desc->length)` read, added a corresponding `smp_rmb()` (read memory barrier).

### Relationship Between Modifications

The patch fixes a memory ordering/data race between the interrupt callback (`wdm_in_callback`) and the read system call (`wdm_read`). The core issue is that without explicit ordering, the compiler or CPU could reorder the update of `desc->length` before the completion of the `memmove` that writes data into the buffer. This would cause `wdm_read()` to observe an increased length but read stale or uninitialized data from the buffer.

- The write-side barrier (`smp_wmb`) and `WRITE_ONCE` ensure that **all writes to the buffer (via `memmove`) are globally visible before the new `desc->length` value becomes visible**.
- The read-side barrier (`smp_rmb`) paired with the write barrier ensures that **when `wdm_read()` sees the new `desc->length`, it is guaranteed to also see the corresponding buffer data** that was written before that length update. The `READ_ONCE` on the read side prevents compiler optimizations that might re-read the value.

Thus, the two barriers form a proper store-load ordering pair that prevents the reordering and eliminates the data race, thereby fixing the potential use of uninitialized memory in `copy_to_user()`.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
memmove(desc->ubuf + desc->length, desc->inbuf, length);
desc->length += length;
```
Reason:
Without proper ordering, the update to `desc->length` can be reordered before the `memmove` due to compiler optimization or CPU out-of-order execution. This causes `wdm_read()` to read the new `desc->length` (via `cntr = desc->length` or later `cntr = READ_ONCE(desc->length)`) while the data in `desc->ubuf` has not been fully copied by `memmove`, leading to `copy_to_user()` copying uninitialized memory.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
smp_wmb(); /* against wdm_read() */
WRITE_ONCE(desc->length, desc->length + length);
```
and
```
cntr = READ_ONCE(desc->length);
smp_rmb(); /* against wdm_in_callback() */
```
Reason:
- `smp_wmb()` ensures that the `memmove` (all prior writes) completes before the store to `desc->length` becomes visible to other CPUs/cores.
- `WRITE_ONCE` prevents the compiler from tearing or reordering the length update.
- `READ_ONCE(desc->length)` in `wdm_read()` ensures a single atomic read of the length.
- `smp_rmb()` ensures that the read of `desc->length` is ordered before subsequent reads of `desc->ubuf` (via `copy_to_user`), so that the reader sees the data written by `memmove` before the length update. Together, these barriers enforce the correct order: data written, then length updated; and reader sees length, then reads data.
